moves.name: Write tomorrow's list before bed
moves.what: Five minutes: everything you need to do tomorrow, on paper, then close the notebook.

source.who: Scullin, Krueger, Ballard, Pruett and Bliwise
source.what: Bedtime writing of to-do lists shortened time to fall asleep by about nine minutes in a sleep-lab study of 57 adults

prior.note: Scullin 2018: writing tomorrow’s list cut sleep onset by about nine minutes against writing a done list; about a third of a step on sleep quality

moves.name: No caffeine after midday
moves.what: Decide it at breakfast: the last coffee, tea or cola before noon today.

source.what: Caffeine taken even six hours before bed cut measured sleep by about an hour, in a crossover study of 12 adults; the basis of the six-hour sleep-hygiene rule

prior.note: Drake 2013: caffeine six hours before bed cut measured sleep by about an hour; about four tenths of a step on sleep quality

moves.name: Phone out of the bedroom
moves.what: Charge it in another room tonight; if you read in bed, read paper.

source.what: Reading on a light-emitting screen before bed delayed melatonin and sleep and dulled next-morning alertness, in a 12-person crossover study

prior.note: Chang 2015: a lit screen before bed delayed melatonin and dulled the next morning; about a third of a step

moves.name: Dim the lights an hour before bed
moves.what: Lamps instead of ceiling lights for the last hour, screens turned down.

source.what: Review of how evening light shifts the body clock and suppresses melatonin, and how dim evenings help

prior.note: Blume 2019 review: evening light pushes the clock later; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Same lights-out time tonight
moves.what: Name the time now and keep it, whatever the evening does.

source.who: Irish, Kline, Gunn, Buysse and Hall
source.what: Review of sleep-hygiene evidence: a regular schedule is among the better-supported habits

prior.note: Irish 2015 review: regular timing is among the best-supported sleep habits; about a third of a step

moves.name: Dinner earlier and lighter
moves.what: Finish eating three hours before lights-out, and keep it to one plate.

source.who: Crispim, Zimberg, dos Reis, Diniz, Tufik and de Mello
source.what: Eating late and heavily near bedtime went with worse sleep quality in 52 healthy adults, measured overnight

prior.note: Crispim 2011: late, heavy meals went with worse sleep; about a fifth of a step, thin

moves.name: A ten-minute walk, now
moves.what: Out the door with no destination, back in ten minutes.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 15 cohorts, 191,130 people: even half the recommended weekly activity went with 18 percent lower depression risk, with the biggest gains at the lowest volumes

prior.note: Reed and Ones 2006: one bout of light activity lifts positive affect by about half a standard deviation; about four tenths of a step on mood

moves.name: Walk somewhere green
moves.what: A park, a river path or trees, for thirty minutes if you have it.

source.who: Bratman, Hamilton, Hahn, Daily and Gross
source.what: A 90-minute walk in nature lowered rumination and activity in the brain region tied to it, unlike the same walk in traffic, in 38 adults

prior.note: Bratman 2015: a ninety-minute nature walk cut rumination against an urban walk; about half a step on overwhelm

moves.name: Walk after dinner
moves.what: Ten minutes on your feet straight after the evening meal.

source.what: Ten minutes of walking after each meal lowered post-meal blood sugar 12 percent more than the same walking at other times, in 41 adults with type 2 diabetes

prior.note: Reynolds 2016 on glucose; on mood the light-activity estimate applies; about a third of a step

moves.name: One set of something hard
moves.what: Push-ups, squats or a plank, to the edge, one set, then stop.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 49 prospective studies: physical activity protects against later depression across ages and regions; a single set is the smallest dose of that

prior.note: Schuch 2018 and Gordon 2018: resistance training lowers low mood over weeks; one set today, about a fifth of a step on energy

moves.name: Ten minutes of daylight before ten
moves.what: Outside, no sunglasses, coffee optional, within an hour or two of waking.

source.who: Wright, McHill, Birks, Griffin, Rusterholz and Chinoy
source.what: A week of natural light and no electric light pulled the body clock two hours earlier in 8 adults; morning light is the anchor

prior.note: Wright 2013: a week of natural light moved the body clock two hours earlier; about a third of a step on next-morning sleep quality

moves.name: Two minutes hard
moves.what: Stairs, a sprint or fast jumping jacks for two minutes, then done.

source.what: Review: a single bout of exercise lifts mood and sharpens attention for up to about two hours afterwards

prior.note: Basso and Suzuki 2017 review: one bout raises arousal and mood for up to two hours; about a third of a step on energy

moves.name: Five minutes of stretching
moves.what: Neck, hips and hamstrings, slowly, breathing out into each one.

source.what: Widely recommended for stiffness and calm; direct evidence on mood is thin

prior.note: Common practice; starts almost flat, about a tenth of a step

moves.name: Finish the shower cold
moves.what: The last thirty seconds of the morning shower cold, and out.

source.who: Buijze, Sierevelt, van der Heijden, Dijkgraaf and Frings-Dresen
source.what: Trial of 3,018 adults: a hot-to-cold shower cut sickness absence by 29 percent; it did not change illness days, and mood was not the outcome

prior.note: Buijze 2016: cold showers cut sick days by 29 percent; on energy the evidence is self-report; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Five minutes of cyclic sighing
moves.what: Two breaths in through the nose, one long slow breath out through the mouth, for five minutes.

source.what: Trial of 108 adults: five minutes a day of cyclic sighing improved mood and lowered breathing rate more than mindfulness or two other breathing patterns over a month

replaces: slow breathing at six a minute

prior.note: Balban 2023: five minutes a day beat mindfulness on positive affect over a month; about four tenths of a step on stress

moves.name: Cold water on the face
moves.what: Thirty seconds of cold water on the face, or a cold cloth held to the side of the neck.

source.who: Jungmann, Vencatachellum, Van Ryckeghem and Vögele
source.what: Cold on the side of the neck raised heart-rate variability and lowered heart rate, a calming shift, in a trial of 61 adults; mood itself was not measured

prior.note: Jungmann 2018: facial cooling slows the heart; on felt stress the evidence is thin; about a tenth of a step

moves.name: Say what you feel in one sentence
moves.what: Out loud or on paper, the feeling and its cause, plainly, once.

source.who: Lieberman, Eisenberger, Crockett, Tom, Pfeifer and Way
source.what: Putting a feeling into words dampened the brain's alarm response in a scanner study of 30 adults

prior.note: Lieberman 2007: labelling an emotion damped the amygdala; about a fifth of a step on irritation

moves.name: Empty your head onto a page
moves.what: Three minutes, everything on your mind, in no order, then put it down.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 146 expressive-writing studies: small but real benefits for wellbeing and distress

prior.note: Frattaroli 2006 meta-analysis: expressive writing, a small effect; about a fifth of a step on overwhelm

moves.name: Eleven minutes lying still with a guided body scan
moves.what: Lie down, eyes closed, a recorded yoga-nidra or body-scan guide, eleven minutes.

source.what: An 11-minute yoga nidra recording used for 30 days lowered stress and improved sleep and wellbeing a little, against a waiting list, in 771 people

prior.note: Moszeik 2022: an eleven-minute yoga nidra cut stress and improved sleep; about a third of a step

moves.name: Talk to yourself by name
moves.what: For a minute, describe the situation as you would to a friend, using your own name instead of I.

source.what: Seven studies: using your own name in self-talk regulated emotion under stress and made thoughts less rumination-like

prior.note: Kross 2014: distanced self-talk reduced distress under social stress; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: A full glass of water
moves.what: A full glass now, before anything else.

source.what: Mild dehydration of about 1 percent worsened mood, concentration and headache in 25 women; a matching study found the same in men

prior.note: Armstrong 2012: mild dehydration lowered mood and raised fatigue; about a fifth of a step on energy

moves.name: Protein at breakfast
moves.what: Eggs, yoghurt or beans on the plate, not toast alone.

source.what: A protein-rich breakfast reduced cravings and evening snacking over a week in 20 young women who usually skipped breakfast

prior.note: Leidy 2013: a protein breakfast cut evening snacking; about a fifth of a step on hunger

moves.name: Sit down for a real lunch
moves.what: Twenty minutes, at a table, away from the screen, a plate not a packet.

source.what: Switching off from work during breaks predicts recovery and lower fatigue, in a scale study of 930 workers

prior.note: Sonnentag and Fritz 2007: detachment during breaks predicts recovery; about a fifth of a step on energy

moves.name: No alcohol tonight
moves.what: Water or tea in the evening instead, decided before dinner.

source.what: Review of 27 studies: alcohol helps you fall asleep but breaks up the second half of the night

prior.note: Ebrahim 2013 review: alcohol cuts REM and fragments the second half of the night; about four tenths of a step on sleep quality

moves.name: Eat something real before four
moves.what: Fruit and nuts, or a yoghurt, before the afternoon dip arrives.

source.what: Widely advised for the mid-afternoon slump; direct evidence on mood is thin

prior.note: Common practice; about a tenth of a step

moves.name: Cook one simple meal from scratch
moves.what: Twenty-five minutes, something you already know how to make, for both of you.

source.what: Review of 11 studies: cooking programmes went with better mood and confidence, in mostly small and uncontrolled designs

prior.note: Farmer 2018 review: cooking programmes lifted mood and confidence, mostly uncontrolled; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Open the book for two minutes
moves.what: Open it, read one paragraph, and you are allowed to stop.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 94 studies: deciding exactly when and where to act roughly doubles follow-through on intentions

prior.note: Gollwitzer and Sheeran 2006: if-then plans raise goal attainment, d about 0.65; about a third of a step on motivation

moves.name: Ten minutes of recall, book closed
moves.what: Write what you remember from the last session, then open the book and check.

source.who: Dunlosky, Rawson, Marsh, Nathan and Willingham
source.what: Review of ten learning techniques for the Association for Psychological Science: practice testing rated high utility, rereading and highlighting low

prior.note: Dunlosky 2013: practice testing rated high utility; about a third of a step on confidence

moves.name: One 25-minute block, phone in another room
moves.what: One topic, a timer, no other tabs, the phone out of sight and out of the room.

source.what: Two experiments with about 800 people: a phone merely present on the desk lowered working memory and attention, even face down and silent

prior.note: Ward 2017: the phone’s mere presence taxes working memory; about a third of a step on focus

moves.name: Review last week's topic for ten minutes
moves.what: Not today's topic, an older one, for ten minutes from memory and notes.

source.who: Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted and Rohrer
source.what: Meta-analysis of 254 studies: study spread over time is remembered far better than the same study massed together

prior.note: Cepeda 2006 meta-analysis: spacing beats massing; about a fifth of a step on confidence over seven days

moves.name: Explain one concept aloud as if teaching
moves.what: To the wall, to the mirror or to her, in your own words, until it is clear.

source.who: Bisra, Liu, Nesbit, Salimi and Winne
source.what: Meta-analysis of 64 studies: prompting learners to explain material to themselves improved learning by a medium effect

prior.note: Bisra 2018 meta-analysis: self-explanation, g about 0.55; about a third of a step on confidence

moves.name: Write the exact next study step
moves.what: Which chapter, which page, at what time tomorrow, on one line.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 94 studies: a concrete when-and-where plan is the strongest simple predictor of doing the thing

prior.note: Gollwitzer and Sheeran 2006; about a third of a step on motivation next morning

moves.name: Ten practice questions, timed
moves.what: From the exam bank, against the clock, then mark them honestly.

source.what: Two experiments: testing yourself beat repeated study for remembering a week later, even though it felt worse at the time

prior.note: Roediger and Karpicke 2006: testing beat rereading a week later; about a third of a step on confidence

moves.name: Clear one surface completely
moves.what: The table or the kitchen counter, to bare, and nothing else.

source.what: Three experiments: an orderly room nudged people toward healthier and more conventional choices; disorder nudged toward novelty

prior.note: Vohs 2013 on orderly rooms; on overwhelm the evidence is thin; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Lay out tomorrow's clothes and bags
moves.what: Hers and yours, by the door, before bed.

source.what: Standard advice for smoother mornings with a small child; no direct trial

prior.note: Common practice; about a fifth of a step on next-morning stress

moves.name: One load of washing, start to finish
moves.what: Washed, dried and put away today, the whole loop closed.

source.what: Diary study of 12,000 workday entries: visible progress, even small, was the strongest lift to the inner working day

prior.note: Amabile and Kramer 2011: small progress lifts the inner work life; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Open the windows for ten minutes
moves.what: Every window, ten minutes, fresh air through the place.

source.who: Allen, MacNaughton, Satish, Santanam, Vallarino and Spengler
source.what: Cognitive scores fell as indoor carbon dioxide rose in a controlled office study of 24 people; fresh air reversed it

prior.note: Allen 2016: lower CO2 doubled cognitive scores in a lab; at home about a fifth of a step on focus

moves.name: Message one friend now
moves.what: One real line to one person, not a forward, not a meme.

source.what: Two studies: days with more small interactions, even with acquaintances, were days with more belonging and happiness

prior.note: Sandstrom and Dunn 2014: even loose-tie contact lifts belonging; about a fifth of a step on loneliness

moves.name: Call someone for ten minutes
moves.what: Voice, not text, with someone you have not spoken to in a while.

source.what: Four experiments: people expected a call to be awkward, but voice built more connection than text with no extra awkwardness

prior.note: Kumar and Epley 2021: people expected calls to be awkward and found them warmer; about a third of a step

moves.name: Send a thank-you to someone who helped
moves.what: Three specific sentences to one person, sent today.

source.what: Three experiments: writers of gratitude letters underestimated how surprised and pleased recipients felt, and overestimated the awkwardness

prior.note: Kumar and Epley 2018: senders underestimated how much thanks landed; about a third of a step on mood

moves.name: Time with her, no agenda
moves.what: Fifteen minutes where she leads and you follow, phone in another room. Not teaching: practising a skill with her is a different move.

source.what: Meta-analysis of parent-child interaction therapy, whose core is daily child-led play: fewer behaviour problems and less parent stress across 24 studies

prior.note: Thomas and Zimmer-Gembeck 2007 meta-analysis; on your own mood, about a third of a step this evening

moves.name: One sentence past hello
moves.what: With the cashier, a neighbour or a parent at pick-up: hello, then one more sentence.

source.what: Nine experiments, train and bus commuters: people expected talking to a stranger to be unpleasant and found it the opposite

prior.note: Epley and Schroeder 2014: commuters who talked to strangers enjoyed the ride more; about a third of a step

moves.name: Invite someone to something this week
moves.what: Coffee after church, a walk, a game night: one invitation, sent today.

source.what: Meta-analysis of seven studies, 2,304 people: fears about talking to others ran far ahead of how the conversations actually went

prior.note: Sandstrom and Boothby 2021: people avoid initiating and enjoy it when they do; about a fifth of a step over seven days; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Arrive ten minutes early on Saturday and talk to one person
moves.what: Before the service, one conversation with someone you do not usually talk to.

source.what: Review of cohort evidence: regular attendance at services goes with lower depression and higher purpose, partly through the community

prior.note: VanderWeele 2017 review: attendance predicts lower low mood; about a third of a step over seven days

moves.name: A ten-minute nap, alarm set
moves.what: Lie down, eyes closed, alarm at ten minutes, then up.

source.what: Lab study of 24 adults after a short night: a 10-minute nap gave the most alertness for the least grogginess, better than 20 or 30

prior.note: Brooks and Lack 2006: a ten-minute nap improved alertness for over two hours; about four tenths of a step on energy

moves.name: Half an hour with no screens
moves.what: Paper, a bath, a walk, the kitchen: anything but glass, for thirty minutes.

source.what: Psychological detachment, really switching off, is the recovery experience most tied to lower exhaustion in a scale study of 930 workers

prior.note: Sonnentag and Fritz 2007; about a fifth of a step on stress

moves.name: A warm shower or bath an hour before bed
moves.what: Ten minutes of warm water, one to two hours before lights-out.

source.who: Haghayegh, Khoshnevis, Smolensky, Diller and Castriotta
source.what: Meta-analysis of 17 studies: a warm bath or shower one to two hours before bed shortened the time to fall asleep and improved sleep quality

prior.note: Haghayegh 2019 meta-analysis: warm bathing one to two hours before bed sped sleep onset by about ten minutes; about a third of a step

moves.name: Five minutes sitting outside doing nothing
moves.what: A step, a bench or the grass, no phone, five minutes of air.

source.what: Analysis of ten UK studies, 1,252 people: even five minutes of activity in green space lifted mood and self-esteem, with the first minutes counting most

prior.note: Barton and Pretty 2010: five minutes of green exercise lifted mood and self-esteem; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: One album side on purpose
moves.what: Twenty minutes of music you chose, doing nothing else at the same time.

source.what: Review of the neurochemistry of music: listening engages reward and lowers stress hormones across many studies

prior.note: Chanda and Levitin 2013 review: music lowers cortisol and raises dopamine markers; about a third of a step on mood

moves.name: Lights out thirty minutes earlier tonight
moves.what: Decide it now, keep the usual alarm, and go up half an hour sooner.

source.who: Irish, Kline, Gunn, Buysse and Hall
source.what: Review of sleep-hygiene evidence: more time in bed on short nights is the plain lever, and regularity keeps it

prior.note: Irish 2015; about four tenths of a step on sleep hours

moves.name: Do one small new thing today
moves.what: A new route, a new shop, a new recipe, a new bench: one, today.

source.what: Phone-tracked study of 122 people over months: days spent in more varied places were happier days, and the link ran both ways

prior.note: Heller 2020: daily novelty went with higher positive affect; about a third of a step this evening

moves.name: Look at every balance, once
moves.what: Bank, card and cash, one look each, the total written on one line.

source.what: Survey work with thousands of adults: stress about managing money today is a large, separate part of overall wellbeing

prior.note: Netemeyer 2018: financial wellbeing predicts life satisfaction; looking is about a fifth of a step on stress

moves.name: Pay or sort one bill, start to finish
moves.what: The one you have been avoiding, done in one sitting today.

source.what: Diary study of 12,000 workday entries: small, visible progress on a real task was the strongest lift to the day

prior.note: Amabile and Kramer 2011; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Spend nothing today
moves.what: Decided at breakfast: no purchases at all until tomorrow.

source.what: A widely used budgeting habit; no direct trial on mood

prior.note: Common practice; about a tenth of a step

moves.name: List next week's costs on one line each
moves.what: Rent, food, fuel, her things, anything due: one line each, one total.

source.what: National survey of 6,394 adults: people who plan ahead and feel in control of day-to-day money report higher financial wellbeing

prior.note: CFPB 2017: planning ahead is a component of financial wellbeing; about a fifth of a step over seven days

moves.name: Cancel one subscription you do not use
moves.what: Find it, cancel it, screenshot the confirmation, done in one sitting.

source.what: Standard money advice; the relief is plausible and untested

prior.note: Common practice; about a fifth of a step over seven days

moves.name: Eye contact with a stranger
moves.what: Hold a stranger's eyes for a beat, a nod, and move on. A rep, not a result.

source.what: Network meta-analysis of 101 trials: exposure-based cognitive therapy, facing feared social situations in small graded steps, is the best-supported route out of social anxiety

prior.note: Mayo-Wilson 2014: exposure-based work is the strongest treatment for social anxiety; one rep, about a fifth of a step on confidence; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Ten seconds past comfortable
moves.what: In a queue or a conversation, stay ten seconds longer than the urge to leave. A rep, not a result.

source.what: Clinical text on exposure: staying in a feared situation past the urge to escape is what teaches the nervous system it is safe

prior.note: Abramowitz 2019: staying in discomfort teaches that it passes; about a fifth of a step; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Say the thing
moves.what: The opinion, the compliment or the ask you were about to swallow, said once today.

source.what: Review of decades of trials: assertiveness training, practising saying what you mean, is an evidence-based treatment that helps across many problems

prior.note: Speed 2018 review of assertiveness training; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: One low-pressure conversation with a woman
moves.what: Somewhere ordinary, a question and a follow-up, with no aim beyond the conversation itself.

source.what: Meta-analysis of seven studies, 2,304 people: the fears people have before talking to someone new run well ahead of how the talks actually go

prior.note: Sandstrom and Boothby 2021; about a third of a step on confidence; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Ask one follow-up question
moves.what: In any conversation today, ask about the thing the other person just said.

source.who: Huang, Yeomans, Brooks, Minson and Gino
source.what: Speed-dating and lab data: people who asked more follow-up questions were liked more, and rarely knew it

prior.note: Huang 2017: follow-up questions raised liking; about a third of a step on social energy; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Write one line on how the last conversation went, then the liking gap
moves.what: One honest line about how it went, then this beneath it: they probably liked you more than you think.

source.what: Five studies: after talking, people consistently underestimated how much the other person liked them and enjoyed it, the liking gap

prior.note: Boothby 2018: people underestimate how much they were liked; about a fifth of a step on confidence; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Read one verse and sit with it
moves.what: One verse, not a chapter, and a quiet minute after it.

source.what: Review of thousands of studies: religious involvement goes with better mental health in most of them; the evidence for any single act is thin

prior.note: Koenig 2012 review: practice and lower low mood, mostly observational; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Five minutes of prayer
moves.what: Your own words, or none at all, for five minutes.

source.what: Review of 41 observational studies: regular private prayer went with less depression and anxiety and more optimism; none of them could show cause

prior.note: Anderson and Nunnelley 2016 review; about a fifth of a step on stress

moves.name: Write one honest sentence to God
moves.what: The truest thing about today, in one unpolished sentence, on paper.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 146 expressive-writing studies: writing what is true about a hard thing gives small but real benefits

prior.note: Frattaroli 2006; about a fifth of a step

moves.name: Name three things you are grateful for tonight
moves.what: Three specific things from today, said to God or written down.

source.what: Online trial of 411 people: writing three good things nightly lifted happiness for months; later meta-analysis finds the effects modest

prior.note: Seligman 2005: three good things raised happiness for six months; about a third of a step on mood next morning

moves.name: One screen-free hour on Saturday as rest
moves.what: No work, no study, no scrolling, for one hour, on purpose.

source.what: Really switching off predicts recovery in a scale study of 930 workers; the Sabbath is the oldest version of it

prior.note: Sonnentag and Fritz 2007; about a third of a step on stress this evening

moves.name: Finish one thing that is nearly done
moves.what: Pick the task closest to finished and close it, in twenty minutes or less.

source.what: Diary study of 12,000 workday entries: making progress on meaningful work, even small, was the strongest lift to motivation and mood

prior.note: Amabile and Kramer 2011: progress on meaningful work is the strongest daily lift; about a third of a step on mood

moves.name: Three two-minute things, now
moves.what: Three tasks that each take under two minutes, done back to back.

source.what: Getting Things Done: anything under two minutes is done at once rather than tracked; widely used, not trialled

prior.note: Allen 2001, practice; about a fifth of a step on overwhelm

moves.name: Close every tab and app but one
moves.what: Close them all, keep the one you are working in, and do that one.

source.what: Two experiments, about 800 people: what is merely within reach pulls attention even when unused

prior.note: Ward 2017; about a fifth of a step on focus

moves.name: Write the smallest next step of the thing you keep avoiding
moves.what: One line, small enough to do in five minutes, then do only that.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 94 studies: a concrete plan for the next action is the strongest simple predictor of taking it

prior.note: Gollwitzer and Sheeran 2006; about a third of a step on motivation

moves.name: Reply to the one message you have been avoiding
moves.what: Two lines, sent, in the next three minutes.

source.what: Diary study of 12,000 workday entries: closing a small open loop counts as progress, and progress lifts the day

prior.note: Amabile and Kramer 2011; about a fifth of a step on overwhelm

moves.name: Set the alarm for leaving, not arriving
moves.what: One alarm, set once, for the minute you must be out of the door for the thing you are always late to. Arriving is not the cue; leaving is.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 94 studies: if-then plans raised goal attainment with an effect of d about 0.65, strongest for getting started on time

prior.note: A leaving cue is an if-then plan; about a third of a step on stress later that day

moves.name: A fifteen-minute buffer before every appointment
moves.what: Once, in the calendar settings: every new event gets a fifteen-minute reminder and a fifteen-minute travel buffer. The plan stops assuming a clear road.

source.what: Five studies of the planning fallacy: people predicted finishing sooner than they did, even knowing their own history

prior.note: A standing buffer corrects the planning fallacy by default; about a fifth of a step on stress over seven days

moves.name: A bin in the car
moves.what: One small bin that lives in the car, once. The rubbish never becomes a job again.

source.what: Review of habit research: behaviour follows the cues and friction of its context more than intention

prior.note: Friction removed once; on overwhelm the evidence is adjacent; about a tenth of a step

moves.name: Book the appointment you keep putting off, today
moves.what: The dentist, the doctor, the car: one call or one form, today, and it is off the list for good.

source.what: The same meta-analysis: a fixed when-and-where turns an intention into an act

prior.note: One avoided task closed; about a third of a step on overwhelm over seven days

moves.name: Put the one bill you forget on autopay
moves.what: Ten minutes, once, and that bill never needs remembering again.

source.what: Automatic enrolment raised pension participation from 49 to 86 percent: a default does what reminders cannot

prior.note: Defaults hold where reminders lapse; about a fifth of a step on stress over seven days

moves.name: Five no-cook dinners in the cupboard
moves.what: Once: five dinners that need no cooking, for the nights nothing else will happen. Eating is the target; cooking is not.

source.what: Untested; keeps a necessity within reach on the worst evenings

prior.note: A necessity made reachable; about a tenth of a step, thin

moves.name: A toothbrush where you actually are at night
moves.what: A second brush and paste by the bed or the sofa, once. The necessity meets you where the evening ends.

source.what: Habits follow context cues; putting the cue where the behaviour must happen is the cheapest change

prior.note: A necessity made reachable; the reading it moves is a guess until the necessity signal lands; about a tenth of a step

moves.name: A speaker in the bathroom, set up once
moves.what: Music makes the shower a place to be rather than a job. Set it up once; the necessity gets easier every day after.

source.what: Review: music engages reward circuits and lowers cortisol; the setting is adjacent

prior.note: A necessity made pleasant; about a tenth of a step, thin

moves.name: Delete the one app that eats the evening
moves.what: Two minutes, once. Not a limit, not a timer: gone from the phone. Reinstalling is allowed and counts as a decision.

source.what: Randomised trial: limiting social media to thirty minutes a day cut loneliness and low mood over three weeks

prior.note: Less evening scrolling; about a third of a step on sleep quality; energy the next morning is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it

moves.name: Running shoes by the door, always
moves.what: One place, by the door, where the shoes live from now on. The walk starts with the door open.

source.what: Habits follow context cues; the cue by the door is the cheapest one there is

prior.note: Removes one step before every walk; about a tenth of a step on energy over seven days

moves.name: A recurring order for what you keep running out of
moves.what: Nappies, coffee, the thing that is always gone: one recurring order, set up once. The shop stops being a surprise.

source.what: Untested; removes a repeating initiation

prior.note: A necessity made automatic; about a tenth of a step, thin

moves.name: Ask one question in a group
moves.what: In the next group you are in, ask one real question and listen to the whole answer. Audience to participant in one move.

source.who: Huang, Yeomans, Brooks, Minson and Gino
source.what: Asking questions, especially follow-ups, raised how much the asker was liked

prior.note: One rep on the participation ladder; about a fifth of a step on confidence

moves.name: Say one full thought, start to finish
moves.what: One complete thought in a group, without trailing off or handing it away. Counted, never rated.

source.what: Review of assertiveness training: practice speaking fully raises confidence and lowers social distress

prior.note: Rung two; about a fifth of a step on confidence

moves.name: Tell one short story
moves.what: One story under a minute, with a beginning and an end, to people who are there. The rep is the telling, not how it lands.

source.what: Review of decades of trials: assertiveness training, practising saying what you mean in full, is an evidence-based treatment; a short story told to people who are there is that practice, evidence for something adjacent

prior.note: Rung three; about a fifth of a step on confidence

moves.name: Start a topic
moves.what: When the conversation lulls, bring up something new rather than waiting for someone else to. The rung above answering.

source.what: People avoid initiating conversation from fear of the reaction, and enjoy it when they do

prior.note: Rung four, the top; about a fifth of a step on confidence

moves.name: Record one story and listen back once
moves.what: Sixty seconds into the phone, one story you might tell this week; listen once, no notes. A rep that works with nobody home.

source.what: Network meta-analysis of 101 trials: individual cognitive therapy with exposure is the best-supported treatment for social anxiety; rehearsing alone is untested on its own

prior.note: A solo rehearsal; about a fifth of a step on confidence, thin; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Read one page aloud, as if to a room
moves.what: One page of anything, out loud, with the pauses and the emphasis you would use for a room. Voice practice with nobody present.

source.what: Untested; the voice is the part of presence that can be trained alone

prior.note: A solo rep; about a tenth of a step, untested; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Three things about the other person
moves.what: In the next conversation, notice three things about them: what they said, how they said it, what they seem to want. Attention outward, not on yourself.

source.what: Turning attention outward during social exposure cut anxiety and self-consciousness more than exposure alone, in a single-case series of eight

prior.note: External focus is the tested ingredient; about a third of a step on confidence; mood is a target too, so the day’s draw can reach it, on thin evidence

moves.name: Notice it and act anyway
moves.what: Name the pull to avoid in one word, then take the next step with it still there. The urge is allowed to come along.

source.what: Acceptance and commitment therapy: willingness and defusion, with a meta-analysis of 39 trials putting the effect at g about 0.4

prior.note: Willingness in one rep; about a fifth of a step on overwhelm

moves.name: One page of a paper book
moves.what: A paper book, one page or more, in bed or on the sofa, phone in another room. For the late nights with nobody up.

source.what: Randomised trial of 991 people: a week of reading in bed left 42 percent reporting better sleep against 28 percent without

prior.note: Reading in bed against not; about a fifth of a step on sleep quality

moves.name: Three lines about today
moves.what: What happened, what it was like, one thing for tomorrow. Three lines, then closed. Late at night, alone, it puts the day down.

source.what: Meta-analysis of 146 studies of expressive writing: a small, reliable effect on wellbeing

prior.note: A fixed, short form of expressive writing; about a fifth of a step on overwhelm next morning

moves.name: Ten minutes of a thing you like, on purpose
moves.what: Pick one thing you enjoy for its own sake and give it ten whole minutes, phone elsewhere. Pleasure scheduled, not stumbled on.

source.what: The Pleasant Events Schedule: day-to-day mood tracks the number and enjoyment of pleasant activities

prior.note: Behavioural activation’s pleasant event, sized to ten minutes; about a third of a step on mood

replaces: an early night after a party
moves.name: Keep the evening after a big social day empty
moves.what: The evening after a big social event, plan nothing and see no one. A gap on purpose, so the next day starts full.

source.what: A week of acting outgoing raised positive affect for everyone but also tiredness and negative affect for introverts

prior.note: The recovery cost is measured; the gap is the untested remedy; about a fifth of a step on social energy next morning

moves.name: Practise one of her skills together
moves.what: Pick one skill from her list under Aims → Her and do it side by side for ten minutes, then count what she did and how much help she needed. Teaching on purpose: time with her, no agenda, is a different move and stays one.

source.what: Learn the Signs. Act Early. tips and activities for 4 years and 5 years: each milestone practised in everyday play with a parent

prior.note: CDC 2022 tips, practice evidence; on your own mood, about a quarter of a step this evening, read from time with her

moves.name: One story, and she tells what happens next
moves.what: Read one short book she knows and stop before the turn: she says what comes next, then tells the whole thing back with two events. Ten minutes, her words more than yours.

source.who: Mol, Bus, de Jong and Smeets
source.what: Meta-analysis of dialogic parent-child book reading across 16 studies: the child answering and telling during the story lifts expressive vocabulary

replaces: reading to her while she listens
a bedtime story with no questions

prior.note: Mol and colleagues 2008 meta-analysis on her vocabulary; on your own mood, about a quarter of a step this evening

moves.name: One small chore together
moves.what: Matching socks or clearing the table after eating, her hands on it and you beside her, ten minutes. The chore gets done and she did it.

source.what: Learn the Signs. Act Early. tips for 5 years: simple chores at home done together, matching socks or clearing the table

replaces: doing the chore yourself while she watches

prior.note: CDC 2022 tips, practice evidence; on your own mood, about a fifth of a step this evening

moves.name: A game with rules, turns taken
moves.what: A short board or card game with one rule and turns, ten minutes. Counting the spaces counts to ten on the way, and waiting for a turn is the skill.

source.what: Randomised trial of a number board game played with an adult over four short sessions: lasting gains in counting and number knowledge in preschoolers

prior.note: Ramani and Siegler 2008 on her counting; on your own mood, about a quarter of a step this evening
about a third of a step up on mood

source.what: Meta-analysis of 32 studies: contact with nature raised positive affect, g about 0.31, and lowered negative affect a little

learnedTags.name: With people
learnedTags.what: Another person is part of the move.

prior.note: about a fifth of a step up on mood and down on loneliness

source.what: Experience sampling: on days with more social interaction, the same person reported higher wellbeing

prior.note: starts nearly flat; no direct evidence that brevity itself helps

source.what: Review: even brief bouts of activity produce measurable affect gains, so short is not a penalty

prior.note: expected to raise how often a move is done, not the reading; starts flat

source.what: Meta-analysis of 26 trials of behavioural activation: graded, low-threshold activity is what patients complete

prior.note: about a third of a step up on mood

source.what: Pleasant activities and daily mood covary; scheduling them is the oldest active ingredient of behavioural activation

learnedTags.name: Mastery
learnedTags.what: Something got done or got better.

prior.note: about a third of a step up on confidence and mood

source.who: Dimidjian, Barrera, Martell, Muñoz and Lewinsohn
source.what: Review of behavioural activation: mastery activities carry the effect alongside pleasant ones

prior.note: about a third of a step up on mood and down on loneliness

source.who: Reis, Sheldon, Gable, Roscoe and Ryan
source.what: Daily diaries: days with more relatedness were better days for the same person

learnedTags.name: Intensity
learnedTags.what: Low, medium or high demand on the body or the nerve.

prior.note: medium about a third of a step, low about a tenth, high about a fifth with a dip while it lasts

source.what: Review: moderate intensity feels good during and after; vigorous feels worse during and better after

filterTags.name: Cost to assign
filterTags.what: What being given this move costs you in time, energy, money or social risk: low, medium or high. Everything the app might assign carries one (Rule 16). Shown here; not yet used in selection.

filterTags.name: Starting effort
filterTags.what: The effort to begin: low, medium or high. The top selection field.

filterTags.name: Needs
filterTags.what: Outdoors, kit, another person, a free hour, daylight, quiet. Stated on the card so you can judge it; the app does not yet filter on it.

filterTags.name: Effect window
filterTags.what: When the effect should show: next block, later that day, this evening, next morning, seven days. Later that day is new in this phase.

research.name: Behavioural activation

sources.what: Depression in Context: act from the outside in; schedule by value, not by mood; avoidance is the target
Brief behavioural activation treatment: activity monitoring, then graded scheduling of valued activities
Randomised trial: behavioural activation matched medication and beat cognitive therapy for more severe depression
Meta-analysis of 26 trials: behavioural activation works, delivered simply

contributes: The move comes before the mood: the app offers a move at the reading, never waits for the wish to do it.
Pleasure and mastery as learned tags: the two kinds of activity behavioural activation schedules, with connection added from self-determination theory.
Graded task assignment: the smaller version on a study night, and the low-effort tag as the top filter.
Trigger, response, avoidance pattern to alternative coping: the entry "Notice it and act anyway".
Activity monitoring: the record itself, and the counts under Follow-through.
research.chips: "Nothing landed today" is behavioural activation’s "no mastery or pleasure today" in plain words. The answer shows how many times before and what the following days looked like, from the record, never a verdict.

research.name: Acceptance and commitment therapy, values

sources.what: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: values, committed action, willingness, defusion
Meta-analysis of 39 randomised trials: ACT beat controls with g about 0.4
Values work: chosen directions, never goals to finish, never scored

contributes: Your direction sentence: one chosen line, shown back unchanged, never counted or graded. No values questionnaire, no "what matters to me" list.
Committed action: the protected step above the move, which the reading cannot displace.
Willingness and defusion: "Notice it and act anyway", and the smaller version instead of the skip.
research.chips: "Hard to see the point today" is answered with your direction line and the record, never argued with. The app does not reason with the feeling; it shows what you chose and what you did.

research.name: Self-determination theory

sources.what: Autonomy, competence and relatedness as the three needs that carry motivation and wellbeing

sources.who: Reis, Sheldon, Gable, Roscoe and Ryan
sources.what: Daily diaries: satisfying the three needs in a day predicted that day’s wellbeing
Across cultures, autonomy, competence and relatedness ranked as what made satisfying events satisfying

contributes: The three reward tags map onto the three needs: pleasure alongside competence (mastery) and relatedness (connection).
Autonomy: you always decide; faith is offered never pushed; a chip is a statement, never a command.
Competence without evaluation: counts, never grades, streaks or readiness scores.
research.chips: A chip’s answer names what was done and who was around, from the record, because competence and relatedness are what a day is made of; it never tells you what to feel.

research.name: Meaning in life

sources.what: The Meaning in Life Questionnaire: presence of meaning and search for it are separate things

sources.who: King, Hicks, Krull and Del Gaiso
sources.what: Six studies: positive affect raises the felt meaning of life, day by day
Review: most people rate their lives as meaningful; routine and coherence carry much of it

contributes: Coherence: what the following days looked like, shown from the record when a chip is tapped.
Purpose: the direction line and the protected step.
Significance: the dated counts under Becoming.
Positive affect raises felt meaning, so the calm, factual reply is the therapeutic one; nothing here diagnoses, and the crisis screen stays dropped.
research.chips: "Hard to see the point today" is a report about the day, never a verdict on a life. The reply is the record: the direction line, and the counts of what was done.

extensionPrompt.intro: From Phase 11 the app writes this prompt for itself from what you never take and which situations run short, private items excluded. The format, so you can veto it before the app ever writes one:
extensionPrompt.template:
You are extending the catalogue of moves for Life Mirror, a phone app for one person. Read the record below and write {n} new entries.

THE RECORD
Situations that run short of candidates: {situations: block, lowest reading, band, candidates left}
Moves offered and never done: {moves: name, offered, done}
Families the filters make unreachable: {families: name, the filter that blocks them}
Moves that held up, and where: {moves: name, situation, tier}

THE RULES
No entry says the same or the opposite thing as an existing one; the conflict and replaces fields are enforced in code.
Every entry carries a source (who, what, year) and its strength: strong, moderate, thin or practice.
Learned tags only from: outdoors, with people, short, low effort; pleasure, mastery, connection; intensity. Filter tags: cost to assign, starting effort, needs, effect window.
One line sized to one sitting; minutes and effort to start; which readings it should move, in which direction, over which window.
A reading, never a verdict: none of the six words the build bans; no streaks, no grades.
Nothing personal, no names, and no private item named or implied.

THE OUTPUT
JSON entries matching the catalogue schema, ready to paste into the catalogue for reading and veto.
